creator: Chris Huber Reitz
name: FINRA — Regulatory Notice 24-09: Gen AI and LLMs
quote: The rules apply when member firms use AI, including Gen AI or similar technologies, in the course of their business, just as they apply when member firms use any other technology or tool.
quote_label: FINRA Regulatory Notice 24-09, 'Regulatory Obligations When Using Gen AI Tools' (June 2024)

provenance.verify_status: ok (live read 2026-10-11; 200 headless this run, previously 403)
provenance.note: Segment gap (self-regulatory licensing body for broker-dealers); not screened for fit. 'This Notice does not create new legal or regulatory requirements or new interpretations of existing requirements.' D1=1: under Rule 3110, where Gen AI is part of the supervisory system 'its policies and procedures should address technology governance, including model risk management, data privacy and integrity, reliability and accuracy of the AI model'; no decision-level record. D2=1: the member firm stays accountable under existing rules; no human-authorship requirement. D3=0: Rule 2210 content standards 'apply whether member firms' communications are generated by a human or technology tool' — same standard, no labeling. D4=0: none (threat actors and synthetic data mentioned, no prohibition). D5=1: 'a member firm should evaluate Gen AI tools prior to deploying them'; surveillance example routes AI summaries to 'the member firm's (human) compliance personnel'. D6=1: names 'concerns about accuracy, privacy, bias, intellectual property'. Posture Enabling ('promising opportunities'; rules 'intended to be technology neutral'). c2_fit=partially: technology neutrality is a decision NOT to draw a permit-vs-reserve line, so the line can't track proof economics either way; its one worked example (machine drafts surveillance summaries, humans judge 'potential evidence of malfeasance') does fit. Contrast SEC IM 2017-02 (contradicts), which explicitly blesses machine fiduciary judgment. c3=Evidential (accuracy, reliability).
